record.paper_title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
record.context_brief: Phase diffusion for concave acoustic branch
record.original_question: For a pair-condensed Fermi gas with a concave acoustic branch γ < 0, what is the true finite phase-diffusion coefficient Dλ, if any, once all relevant phonon collision channels are included? A four-phonon small-angle Landau-Khalatnikov treatment conserves the total number of phonons and gives an infinite Dλ with superdiffusive phase spreading, so the unresolved task is to include subdominant five-phonon processes φφ ↔ φφφ and large-angle four-phonon processes consistently.

evidence.quote: In the concave case γ < 0, on the other hand, the question remains largely open. An attempt to calculate Dλ in reference [86], taking into account only the Landau-Khalatnikov four-phonon collision processes φφ → φφ at small angles, of typical rate Γφ coll ∝ (kBT /mc 2)7mc 2/ħ|γ| ≈ T 7, led to an infinite diffusion coefficient

To go beyond this and obtain the true (a priori finite) value of Dλ remains an open question: one would have to take into account the subdominant five-phonon processes φφ ↔ φφφ which change Nφ and occur at a rate ≈ T 9 [96], of the same order of magnitude as that of large-angle φφ → φφ processes [52, 78], which is not easy.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a three-dimensional homogeneous pair-condensed Fermi gas at very low temperature T (with k_B T much less than the pairing gap), so that its low-energy excitations are bosonic phonons with linear dispersion ω_q ≃ c q at small wave number q, where c is the sound velocity and m is the fermion mass. Assume the next-to-linear correction to the acoustic branch is concave, i.e.

  ω_q = c q [1 + (γ/8)(ħ q/(m c))^2 + o(q^2)],   with γ < 0.

Let λ(t) denote the global phase of the order parameter; in a canonical-like ensemble its variance grows in time, and one defines the phase-diffusion coefficient

  D_λ = lim_{t→∞} (1/(2t)) Var[λ(t) − λ(0)],

assuming this limit exists and is finite.

For γ < 0, restricting the phonon collision integral to the small-angle Landau–Khalatnikov four-phonon processes φφ → φφ (which conserve the total phonon number N_φ and have a typical rate ∝ (k_B T/(m c^2))^7 · m c^2/(ħ|γ|) ∝ T^7) yields a divergent D_λ and superdiffusive spreading of λ(t).

Determine the true, finite value of D_λ (or prove its finiteness/infiniteness) when one consistently includes, in addition, the subdominant five-phonon processes φφ ↔ φφφ that do not conserve N_φ (rate ∝ T^9) together with the large-angle four-phonon processes φφ → φφ of comparable order, for a pair-condensed Fermi gas with concave acoustic branch γ < 0.
artifact.category_tag: Phonon kinetics in pair-condensed Fermi gases
artifact.status_search_result: Existing analyses of phonon interactions in pair-condensed Fermi gases (Kurkjian–Castin–Sinatra and follow-ups) treat only the small-angle Landau–Khalatnikov 2↔2 channel for γ<0, which yields a divergent phase-diffusion coefficient. No published computation appears to incorporate both the five-phonon φφ↔φφφ processes and the large-angle four-phonon processes needed to obtain a finite D_λ; the question is described in the literature as remaining largely open.

status_evidence.title: Three-phonon and four-phonon interaction processes in a pair-condensed Fermi gas
status_evidence.snippet: For a concave dispersion at low wave-number, Beliaev-Landau interactions are not resonant, and Landau-Khalatnikov 2↔2 processes dominate.
status_evidence.claim: Only 2↔2 four-phonon processes have been used in the concave case; this leads to the divergent D_λ noted in the question.

status_evidence.title: Étalement de la phase et cohérence temporelle d'un gaz de fermions condensé par paires à basse température
status_evidence.snippet: Variance of the phase shift contains a ballistic, diffusive and exotic sub-subdominant terms; analytical expressions are obtained for some coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: In the concave case, the diffusive coefficient remains undetermined when only small-angle 4-phonon processes are kept.
